checks.title: Attach admin policy to role
checks.grants: Can attach the AdministratorAccess managed policy to this role
checks.why: this principal can call iam:AttachRolePolicy to attach AdministratorAccess (or any managed policy) to role the target. Once this principal can use the target (assume it, or steal its credentials from compute), the target is now an administrator; the attachment persists until removed.
checks.fix: Remove iam:AttachRolePolicy from the principal.

checks.title: Attach admin policy to user
checks.grants: Can attach the AdministratorAccess managed policy to this user
checks.why: this principal can call iam:AttachUserPolicy to attach the managed AdministratorAccess policy (or any powerful managed policy) to user the target. If the target is controlled by this principal this is one-call self-promotion to full admin, and the attachment persists until someone detaches it.
checks.fix: Remove iam:AttachUserPolicy from the principal.

checks.title: Create default policy version
checks.grants: Can create a new default version of this attached managed policy
checks.why: this principal can call iam:CreatePolicyVersion on attached customer-managed policy the target and publish a new version marked as default. That silently rewrites the effective permissions of every principal the target is attached to, including this principal itself, so this principal can grant itself full administrator access in a single call. AWS-managed policies are immune (they cannot be versioned), which is why only customer-managed policies are targeted.
checks.fix: Remove iam:CreatePolicyVersion from the principal.

checks.title: Create Roles Anywhere profile credentials
checks.grants: Can bind a privileged role to a Roles Anywhere profile and create creds from an external cert
checks.why: this principal can call rolesanywhere:CreateProfile to bind privileged role the target to an IAM Roles Anywhere profile, then present a certificate chained to a registered trust anchor to create that role's credentials from outside AWS. This survives IAM credential rotation and is durable persistence.
checks.fix: Restrict rolesanywhere:CreateProfile and iam:PassRole for roles trusting rolesanywhere.amazonaws.com to a break-glass role.

checks.title: EC2 CreateFleet passrole exec
checks.grants: Can launch an EC2 fleet with an instance profile and reach its IMDS credentials
checks.why: this principal can call ec2:CreateFleet with a launch template carrying instance-profile role the target, launching instances whose IMDS exposes the target's credentials. Standard IMDS/user-data code-exec as the passed role.
checks.fix: Scope iam:PassRole for roles trusting ec2.amazonaws.com; restrict ec2:CreateFleet.

mitre.name: Modify Cloud Compute Infrastructure: Create Cloud Instance

checks.title: EKS node group passrole exec
checks.grants: Can create an EKS managed node group whose EC2 node role creds are attacker-reachable
checks.why: this principal can call eks:CreateNodegroup passing node role the target. The managed nodes are ordinary EC2 instances exposing the target via IMDS, and node roles are frequently broad (ECR, CNI, SSM, plus app policies).
checks.fix: Scope iam:PassRole for the node role (trusts ec2.amazonaws.com); restrict eks:CreateNodegroup.

mitre.name: Modify Cloud Compute Infrastructure: Create Cloud Instance

checks.title: EKS Pod Identity passrole
checks.grants: Can bind a privileged role to an attacker pod via a new Pod Identity association
checks.why: this principal can call eks:CreatePodIdentityAssociation to map privileged role the target onto a service account it controls, then run a pod as that account to assume the target through the EKS Pod Identity agent.
checks.fix: Scope iam:PassRole for roles trusting pods.eks.amazonaws.com; restrict eks:CreatePodIdentityAssociation to cluster admins.

checks.title: Hijack App Runner service role
checks.grants: Can reconfigure this App Runner service to run attacker code as its instance role
checks.why: this principal can call apprunner:UpdateService on an existing App Runner service that already carries instance role the target, reconfiguring it to run attacker-controlled code, a malicious StartCommand, a container image with a web shell, or a repository with a malicious apprunner.yaml. On the next deployment App Runner runs that code as the target, no iam:PassRole and no apprunner:CreateService needed, because the target is already bound to the service. The code reads the target's live credentials from the runtime environment or calls AWS directly; if the target is privileged this is full privilege escalation against a service that was already trusted.
checks.fix: Restrict apprunner:UpdateService on services that carry a privileged instance role; review source/image config changes.

checks.title: Hijack Batch job-definition role
checks.grants: Can submit this Batch job with an override command and run a container as its job role
checks.why: this principal can call batch:SubmitJob against an existing Batch job definition that already carries job role the target, supplying a ContainerOverrides.Command whose shell command is attacker-controlled. Batch runs that command in a container as the target, no iam:PassRole and no batch:RegisterJobDefinition needed, because the target is already bound to the job definition. The command reads the target's live credentials from the task-metadata endpoint or calls AWS directly; if the target is privileged this is full privilege escalation against a job definition that was already trusted.
checks.fix: Restrict batch:SubmitJob on job queues/definitions that carry a privileged jobRoleArn; disallow ContainerOverrides.Command.

checks.title: Hijack CloudFormation stack role
checks.grants: Can update this stack's template and run changes as its existing service role
checks.why: this principal can call cloudformation:UpdateStack on the target, which already carries a privileged service role. By pushing a modified template, this principal makes CloudFormation execute its changes using the target's existing service role, no iam:PassRole needed, because the role is already bound to the stack. A privileged service role means the attacker's template can provision admin resources: full privilege escalation.
checks.fix: Restrict cloudformation:UpdateStack on stacks that carry a privileged service role.

checks.title: Hijack CloudFormation stack role via change set
checks.grants: Can execute a malicious change set on this stack as its existing service role
checks.why: this principal can call cloudformation:CreateChangeSet and cloudformation:ExecuteChangeSet on an existing CloudFormation stack that already carries service role the target. By staging a modified template as a change set and executing it, this principal makes CloudFormation apply the attacker's changes using the target, no iam:PassRole needed, because the target is already bound to the stack. A privileged service role means the attacker's template can provision admin resources: full privilege escalation against a stack that was already trusted.
checks.fix: Restrict cloudformation:CreateChangeSet/ExecuteChangeSet on stacks that carry a privileged service role.

checks.title: Hijack CodeBuild project role
checks.grants: Can start this CodeBuild project with override commands as its service role
checks.why: this principal can call codebuild:StartBuild on an existing CodeBuild project that already carries service role the target, supplying a buildspecOverride whose shell commands are attacker-controlled. CodeBuild runs those commands on its managed infrastructure as the target, no iam:PassRole and no codebuild:CreateProject needed, because the target is already bound to the project. The commands read the target's live credentials from the build environment or call AWS directly; if the target is privileged this is full privilege escalation against a project that was already trusted.
checks.fix: Restrict codebuild:StartBuild on projects that carry a privileged service role; disallow buildspec overrides.

checks.title: Hijack CodeBuild project role (batch)
checks.grants: Can start a batch build on this project with override commands as its service role
checks.why: this principal can call codebuild:StartBuildBatch on an existing CodeBuild project that already carries service role the target, supplying a buildspecOverride whose shell commands are attacker-controlled. CodeBuild runs those commands on its managed infrastructure as the target, no iam:PassRole and no codebuild:CreateProject needed, because the target is already bound to the project. The commands read the target's live credentials from the build environment or call AWS directly; if the target is privileged this is full privilege escalation against a project that was already trusted.
checks.fix: Restrict codebuild:StartBuildBatch on projects that carry a privileged service role; disallow buildspec overrides.

checks.title: Hijack EC2 user-data
checks.grants: Can rewrite this instance's user-data and run code as its instance-profile role
checks.why: this principal can stop the target, rewrite its user-data with ec2:ModifyInstanceAttribute, and start it again; on boot the instance runs the attacker's user-data script as its already-attached instance-profile role, no iam:PassRole needed. A privileged instance profile means arbitrary code execution as that role: full privilege escalation against a box that was already trusted.
checks.fix: Restrict ec2:ModifyInstanceAttribute on instances with attached instance profiles.

checks.title: Hijack Glue dev endpoint role
checks.grants: Can inject an SSH key into this Glue dev endpoint and run a session as its role
checks.why: this principal can call glue:UpdateDevEndpoint on an existing Glue development endpoint that already carries role the target, injecting an attacker SSH public key (addPublicKeys) or custom libraries. The attacker then SSHes into the endpoint and gets an interactive session that runs as the target, no iam:PassRole needed, because the target is already bound to the endpoint. The session reads the target's live temporary credentials directly; if the target is privileged this is full privilege escalation against a resource that was already trusted.
checks.fix: Restrict glue:UpdateDevEndpoint on dev endpoints that carry a privileged role; disallow adding SSH public keys / custom libraries to existing endpoints.

checks.title: Hijack instance role via SSM command
checks.grants: Can run a command on this instance via SSM and steal its instance-profile role
checks.why: this principal can call ssm:SendCommand to run an AWS-RunShellScript document on an SSM-managed instance that already carries instance-profile role the target, executing attacker commands that read the target's live credentials from IMDS and ship them out, non-interactively, with no shell session, key, or open port. Because the target is already bound to the box, command execution on it is enough to steal the role, no iam:PassRole needed. If the target is privileged this is full privilege escalation against an instance that was already trusted, and it is scriptable across many instances at once.
checks.fix: Restrict ssm:SendCommand to break-glass principals; reduce the instance-profile role's permissions.

checks.title: Hijack instance role via SSM session
checks.grants: Can open an SSM shell on this instance and steal its instance-profile role
checks.why: this principal can call ssm:StartSession to open an interactive Session Manager shell on an SSM-managed instance that already carries instance-profile role the target, then read the target's live credentials from the instance metadata service (IMDS). No SSH key, no open security-group port, and no write to the instance, because the target is already bound to the box a shell on it is enough to steal the role. If the target is privileged this is full privilege escalation against an instance that was already trusted.
checks.fix: Restrict ssm:StartSession to break-glass principals; reduce the instance-profile role's permissions.

checks.title: Hijack Lambda function code
checks.grants: Can overwrite this function's code and run it as its execution role
checks.why: this principal can call lambda:UpdateFunctionCode on an existing function that runs as the target, overwriting the function's deployment package with attacker-controlled code. On the next invocation that code executes with the target's permissions and reads the target's live credentials from the Lambda runtime environment, no iam:PassRole needed, because the target is already bound to the function. If the target is privileged this is full privilege escalation against a function that was already trusted.
checks.fix: Restrict lambda:UpdateFunctionCode to CI/CD principals; reduce the function execution role's permissions.

checks.title: Hijack Lambda function configuration
checks.grants: Can attach a malicious layer to this function and run code as its execution role
checks.why: this principal can call lambda:UpdateFunctionConfiguration on an existing function that runs as the target, attaching an attacker-controlled Lambda layer (or changing the runtime, handler, or environment) so that attacker code loads on the next invocation, without overwriting the function's published code. That code executes with the target's permissions and reads the target's live credentials from the Lambda runtime environment, no iam:PassRole needed, because the target is already bound to the function. If the target is privileged this is full privilege escalation against a function that was already trusted.
checks.fix: Restrict lambda:UpdateFunctionConfiguration to CI/CD principals; reduce the function execution role's permissions.

checks.title: Hijack SageMaker notebook via lifecycle config
checks.grants: Can attach a startup script to this notebook and run code as its execution role
checks.why: this principal can create a notebook lifecycle configuration with an attacker-controlled startup script, stop an existing notebook that runs as the target, attach the config with sagemaker:UpdateNotebookInstance, and start the notebook again. On startup the script executes as the target and reads the target's live credentials, no iam:PassRole needed, because the target is already bound to the notebook. If the target is privileged this is full privilege escalation against a notebook that was already trusted.
checks.fix: Restrict sagemaker:UpdateNotebookInstance / lifecycle-config actions on notebooks that carry a privileged execution role.

checks.title: Hijack SageMaker notebook via presigned URL
checks.grants: Can create a presigned URL to this notebook and run a shell as its execution role
checks.why: this principal can call sagemaker:CreatePresignedNotebookInstanceUrl on an existing notebook instance that runs as the target, creating a signed URL that opens the notebook's Jupyter environment. Using Jupyter's built-in terminal, a shell running as the target, the attacker reads the target's live credentials or calls AWS directly. No iam:PassRole is needed, because the target is already bound to the notebook. If the target is privileged this is full privilege escalation against a notebook that was already trusted.
checks.fix: Restrict sagemaker:CreatePresignedNotebookInstanceUrl to operators; reduce the notebook execution role's permissions.

checks.title: Hijack Step Functions state-machine role
checks.grants: Can rewrite this state machine and call AWS directly as its execution role
checks.why: this principal can call states:UpdateStateMachine on an existing Step Functions state machine that already carries execution role the target, replacing its ASL definition with one whose SDK-integration task calls AWS directly (e.g. iam:AttachUserPolicy), then states:StartExecution to run it. The task executes as the target, no iam:PassRole and no states:CreateStateMachine needed, because the target is already bound to the state machine. If the target is privileged this is full privilege escalation against a state machine that was already trusted.
checks.fix: Restrict states:UpdateStateMachine / states:StartExecution on state machines that carry a privileged execution role.

checks.title: Put inline role policy
checks.grants: Can write an inline admin policy directly onto this role
checks.why: this principal can call iam:PutRolePolicy to write an inline policy onto role the target, granting it any permissions, typically full admin. Once this principal can reach the target (assume it, or steal its credentials via compute), the inline grant turns the target into an administrator and persists until removed.
checks.fix: Remove iam:PutRolePolicy from the principal.

checks.title: Put inline user policy
checks.grants: Can write an inline admin policy directly onto this user
checks.why: this principal can call iam:PutUserPolicy to write an inline policy directly onto user the target, granting it any permissions it wants, typically a full administrator allow. If the target is a user this principal controls (often itself), this is immediate self-promotion to admin and the granted policy persists until removed.
checks.fix: Remove iam:PutUserPolicy from the principal.

checks.title: Roll back default policy version
checks.grants: Can roll this attached managed policy back to a more-permissive saved version
checks.why: this principal can call iam:SetDefaultPolicyVersion on attached customer-managed policy the target to promote one of its non-default stored versions to the default. IAM keeps up to five versions of a policy; if an older, more-permissive version exists (for example a prior admin grant), rolling it back to default silently widens the effective permissions of every principal the target is attached to, including this principal itself, with no new policy document written. AWS-managed policies cannot be versioned, so only customer-managed policies are targeted.
checks.fix: Remove iam:SetDefaultPolicyVersion from the principal; prune stale permissive policy versions.

checks.title: SageMaker model/endpoint passrole exec
checks.grants: Can pass a role into a SageMaker model+endpoint and run an attacker container as it
checks.why: this principal can call sagemaker:CreateModel passing execution role the target with an attacker-controlled container image, then CreateEndpointConfig + CreateEndpoint to run it. The container executes as the target and can exfiltrate its credentials.
checks.fix: Scope iam:PassRole for roles trusting sagemaker.amazonaws.com; restrict sagemaker:CreateModel.

checks.title: SageMaker tuning job passrole exec
checks.grants: Can pass a role into a SageMaker tuning job and run an attacker container as it
checks.why: this principal can call sagemaker:CreateHyperParameterTuningJob passing role the target, launching attacker-controlled training containers that execute as the target.
checks.fix: Scope iam:PassRole for roles trusting sagemaker.amazonaws.com; restrict sagemaker:CreateHyperParameterTuningJob.

checks.title: Add self to privileged group
checks.grants: Can add itself to this privileged group and inherit its permissions
checks.why: this principal can call iam:AddUserToGroup to add itself (or a user it controls) to privileged group the target, inheriting all of the target's permissions without touching any policy document. If the target already carries strong access this is instant privilege escalation, and the membership persists until revoked.
checks.fix: Remove iam:AddUserToGroup from the principal.

checks.title: Assign self to admin permission set
checks.grants: Can assign a principal to an already-provisioned admin permission set
checks.why: this principal can call sso:CreateAccountAssignment to bind an attacker-controlled principal to permission set the target in a target account. If that set is already provisioned as an admin (e.g. AdministratorAccess), the assignment hands the attacker a federated admin role with no policy edit at all - the cleanest real-world Identity Center privesc.
checks.fix: Restrict sso:CreateAccountAssignment to a break-glass Identity Center admin; alarm on new assignments to privileged permission sets.

checks.title: Associate instance profile (IMDS steal)
checks.grants: Can attach this role's instance profile to an EC2 instance and steal its credentials via IMDS
checks.why: this principal holds iam:PassRole on the target together with ec2:AssociateIamInstanceProfile, so it can attach the target's instance profile to an EC2 instance it controls and then read the role's temporary credentials from IMDS. Unlike ec2:RunInstances this needs no new instance: it re-points an existing box at a more privileged role, which is quieter and cheaper.
checks.fix: Remove iam:PassRole for this role or scope it with iam:PassedToService; restrict ec2:AssociateIamInstanceProfile / ReplaceIamInstanceProfileAssociation.

mitre.name: Unsecured Credentials: Cloud Instance Metadata API

checks.title: Attach admin policy to group
checks.grants: Can attach the AdministratorAccess managed policy to this group
checks.why: this principal can call iam:AttachGroupPolicy to attach AdministratorAccess (or any managed policy) to group the target, promoting every member, including this principal if it belongs to the target, in a single call. The attachment persists until removed.
checks.fix: Remove iam:AttachGroupPolicy from the principal.

checks.title: Attach admin to Identity Center permission set
checks.grants: Can attach AdministratorAccess to a provisioned permission set and push it
checks.why: this principal can call sso:AttachManagedPolicyToPermissionSet to add AdministratorAccess to permission set the target, then sso:ProvisionPermissionSet to push the change into every account the set is assigned to, turning a scoped federated role into an org-wide administrator.
checks.fix: Restrict sso:AttachManagedPolicyToPermissionSet / ProvisionPermissionSet to a break-glass role; alarm on the events.

checks.title: Bind role to Cognito Identity Pool
checks.grants: Can bind this role to a Cognito Identity Pool and redeem its credentials
checks.why: this principal holds iam:PassRole on the target plus cognito-identity:SetIdentityPoolRoles, so it can bind the target as a Cognito Identity Pool's (unauthenticated) role and then redeem temporary credentials for the target via GetId + GetCredentialsForIdentity. Because the target trusts cognito-identity.amazonaws.com (AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity) the binding is accepted; if the target is privileged this is full privilege escalation, reachable even by an anonymous caller.
checks.fix: Remove iam:PassRole / cognito-identity:SetIdentityPoolRoles; scope identity-pool roles and disable unauthenticated access.

checks.title: Create account and assume admin
checks.grants: Can create a member account and assume its default admin role
checks.why: this principal can call organizations:CreateAccount to spin up a fresh member account whose default OrganizationAccountAccessRole trusts the management account, then assume into it as admin - durable, low-visibility persistence.
checks.fix: Restrict organizations:CreateAccount to a break-glass role; alarm on new account creation.

checks.title: Detach SCP guardrail
checks.grants: Can detach an SCP guardrail from an account or OU
checks.why: this principal can call organizations:DetachPolicy to detach an SCP guardrail from an account or OU, removing an org-wide Deny the rest of the model relies on.
checks.fix: Restrict organizations:DetachPolicy to a break-glass management-account role; alarm on SCP detachment.

mitre.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools

checks.title: Disable S3 Block Public Access
checks.grants: Can disable Block Public Access, enabling a public policy or ACL to take effect
checks.why: this principal can call s3:PutBucketPublicAccessBlock on bucket the target to turn off Block Public Access, so a public bucket policy or ACL grant is no longer overridden and actually exposes the data.
checks.fix: Remove s3:PutBucketPublicAccessBlock / PutAccountPublicAccessBlock from the principal; keep account-level BPA on and deny changes via SCP.

checks.title: EKS access-entry cluster-admin
checks.grants: Can map itself onto this EKS cluster as Kubernetes cluster-admin, reaching its AWS roles
checks.why: this principal can call eks:CreateAccessEntry to map its own IAM principal onto cluster the target, then eks:AssociateAccessPolicy (AmazonEKSClusterAdminPolicy) to become Kubernetes cluster-admin - of a cluster it had no prior access to. Cluster-admin can schedule a pod as any service account, reaching the node-group role, every IRSA role, and every Pod Identity role the cluster fronts.
checks.fix: Restrict eks:CreateAccessEntry / eks:AssociateAccessPolicy to a break-glass role; require CONFIG_MAP-only auth on sensitive clusters; alarm on new access entries.

checks.title: Enroll attacker MFA on user
checks.grants: Can enroll an attacker-controlled MFA device on this user
checks.why: this principal can call iam:CreateVirtualMFADevice then iam:EnableMFADevice to bind an attacker-controlled MFA device to user the target, establishing persistence that survives credential rotation.
checks.fix: Remove iam:CreateVirtualMFADevice / iam:EnableMFADevice from the principal; alarm on new MFA enrolments.

checks.title: Escalate Identity Center permission set
checks.grants: Can rewrite this Identity Center permission set to grant its provisioned role full admin
checks.why: this principal can call sso:PutInlinePolicyToPermissionSet to attach an inline *:* policy to the IAM Identity Center permission set provisioned as role the target, then sso:ProvisionPermissionSet to push it. AWS rewrites the AWSReservedSSO_* role's policy in EVERY account that permission set is assigned to, so a single API call turns a scoped federated role into an administrator org-wide, and the grant persists until the permission set is repaired.
checks.fix: Remove sso:PutInlinePolicyToPermissionSet / ProvisionPermissionSet from the principal; restrict Identity Center administration to a break-glass role.

checks.title: Grant bucket read via ACL
checks.grants: Can rewrite this bucket's ACL to grant public or attacker read
checks.why: this principal can call s3:PutBucketAcl on bucket the target to grant READ to AllUsers, AuthenticatedUsers, or an external canonical id, then read the objects. An alternate exposure path to the bucket-policy grant.
checks.fix: Remove s3:PutBucketAcl from the principal; enforce Object Ownership = BucketOwnerEnforced (disables ACLs) and Block Public Access.

checks.title: Grant object read via ACL
checks.grants: Can rewrite object ACLs to grant public or attacker read
checks.why: this principal can call s3:PutObjectAcl on objects in bucket the target to grant READ to AllUsers/AuthenticatedUsers/an external id, then read them.
checks.fix: Remove s3:PutObjectAcl from the principal; enforce Object Ownership = BucketOwnerEnforced and Block Public Access.

checks.title: Grant org access via resource policy
checks.grants: Can grant an external/member principal management access to the org
checks.why: this principal can call organizations:PutResourcePolicy to grant an external or member principal management access to the organization via its resource policy.
checks.fix: Restrict organizations:PutResourcePolicy to a break-glass management-account role.

checks.title: Hijack Bedrock AgentCore interpreter role
checks.grants: Can invoke Python in this AgentCore interpreter and run it as its execution role
checks.why: this principal can call bedrock-agentcore:StartCodeInterpreterSession and InvokeCodeInterpreter on an existing Bedrock AgentCore code interpreter that already carries execution role the target, and invoke attacker-supplied Python in the session. The interpreter runs that Python in its MicroVM as the target, no iam:PassRole and no CreateCodeInterpreter needed, because the target is already bound to the interpreter. The Python reads the target's live credentials from the MicroVM metadata service or calls AWS directly; if the target is privileged this is full privilege escalation against an interpreter that was already trusted. Marked needs-verification because AgentCore is a brand-new 2025 service and this is a two-action edge.
checks.fix: Restrict bedrock-agentcore:StartCodeInterpreterSession / InvokeCodeInterpreter on interpreters that carry a privileged execution role; scope these actions to specific interpreter ARNs.

checks.title: Hijack CodeDeploy target instance role
checks.grants: Can deploy a malicious revision and run a script as the target instances' role
checks.why: this principal can call codedeploy:CreateDeployment on an existing deployment group whose target EC2 instances already carry instance-profile role the target, deploying a revision whose appspec.yml lifecycle hook runs an attacker shell script as root on those instances. The script reads the target's live credentials from IMDS, no iam:PassRole needed, because the target is already bound to the boxes. If the target is privileged this is full privilege escalation against instances that were already trusted.
checks.fix: Restrict codedeploy:CreateDeployment on deployment groups whose target instances carry a privileged instance profile; review appspec lifecycle hooks.

checks.title: Hijack instance role via Instance Connect
checks.grants: Can push an SSH key via Instance Connect and steal this instance's role
checks.why: this principal can call ec2-instance-connect:SendSSHPublicKey to inject an ephemeral SSH key onto a running instance that already carries instance-profile role the target, then SSH in over the network and read the target's live credentials from IMDS. Because the target is already bound to the box, a shell on it is enough to steal the role, no iam:PassRole needed. Unlike SSM this requires a reachable SSH port (22) on the instance, so it only works where the network path exists; if the target is privileged this is full privilege escalation against an instance that was already trusted.
checks.fix: Restrict ec2-instance-connect:SendSSHPublicKey to break-glass principals; close inbound port 22 and prefer SSM Session Manager.

checks.title: Inject user-data into EC2 launch template
checks.grants: Can inject user-data into this launch template, run as its role on next launch
checks.why: this principal can call ec2:CreateLaunchTemplateVersion to publish a new version of an existing launch template carrying attacker-controlled user-data, then ec2:ModifyLaunchTemplate to set that version as the default, no iam:PassRole needed. The template already references instance-profile role the target, so any instance later launched from it (an Auto Scaling group scaling out, a fleet refresh, or a manual RunInstances) boots the attacker's user-data and runs it as the target, exposing the target's credentials via IMDS. If the target is privileged this is full privilege escalation against a template that was already trusted. NOTE: execution is DEFERRED to a future launch from the template.
checks.fix: Restrict ec2:CreateLaunchTemplateVersion and ec2:ModifyLaunchTemplate on launch templates that reference a privileged instance-profile role; prefer immutable/source-controlled templates.

checks.title: Leave the organization
checks.grants: Can remove the account from the org, escaping every SCP at once
checks.why: this principal can call organizations:LeaveOrganization to remove the account from the org, escaping every SCP that constrained it in one call.
checks.fix: Restrict organizations:LeaveOrganization to a break-glass role; deny for member accounts via SCP.

mitre.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools

checks.title: Open ECS Exec shell
checks.grants: Can open an interactive ECS Exec shell inside this running container
checks.why: this principal can call ecs:ExecuteCommand to open an interactive shell inside running container the target via ECS Exec, no SSH key, no open security-group port, no iam:PassRole, bypassing the network path entirely. That yields code execution inside the container, from which this principal can read the task role's temporary credentials from the ECS task-metadata endpoint and pivot further into the account.
checks.fix: Restrict ecs:ExecuteCommand to break-glass principals; disable ECS Exec (enableExecuteCommand=false) on tasks that don't need it.

checks.title: Open SSM shell
checks.grants: Can open an interactive SSM shell on this instance
checks.why: this principal can call ssm:StartSession to open an interactive shell on SSM-managed instance the target, no SSH key, no open security-group port, bypassing the network path entirely. That yields OS-level code execution on the target, from which this principal can read the instance's IAM role credentials and pivot further into the account.
checks.fix: Restrict ssm:StartSession to break-glass principals only.

checks.title: Pass role to App Runner
checks.grants: Can deploy an App Runner service with this role and run code as it
checks.why: this principal holds iam:PassRole on the target plus apprunner:CreateService, so it can deploy an App Runner service from an attacker-controlled image/source with the target as its instance role, the service's code runs with the target's permissions. Because the target trusts tasks.apprunner.amazonaws.com the pass is accepted; a privileged the target yields run-as-role code execution.
checks.fix: Remove iam:PassRole for this role or scope it with iam:PassedToService.

checks.title: Pass role to Auto Scaling group
checks.grants: Can launch an Auto Scaling instance with this role and run code as it
checks.why: this principal holds iam:PassRole on the target plus autoscaling:CreateLaunchConfiguration and autoscaling:CreateAutoScalingGroup, so it can define a launch configuration that attaches the target as the instance profile and create an Auto Scaling group that boots an EC2 instance from it, the instance runs attacker-supplied user-data as the target and exposes the target's credentials via IMDS. Because the target trusts ec2.amazonaws.com the pass is accepted; if the target is privileged this is full account-level privilege escalation, the Auto Scaling control-plane variant of launching an instance.
checks.fix: Remove iam:PassRole for this role or scope it with iam:PassedToService.

checks.title: Pass role to AWS Batch
checks.grants: Can register and submit an AWS Batch job with this role and run a container as it
checks.why: this principal holds iam:PassRole on the target plus batch:RegisterJobDefinition and batch:SubmitJob, so it can register a Batch job definition with the target as its job role and an attacker-controlled container command, then submit a job, the container runs with the target's permissions and reads the target's credentials from the task-metadata endpoint. checks.why: this principal can call lakeformation:GrantPermissions to grant itself SELECT (or ALL) on governed table the target, then query the table and the S3 data it catalogs. Lake Formation is the authorization layer over the data lake, so self-granting inside it bypasses the absence of a table-level grant: the attacker rewrites the lock rather than holding a key, turning control of the grant API into read access to the governed data.
checks.fix: Restrict lakeformation:GrantPermissions and lakeformation:PutDataLakeSettings to data-lake admins; deny LF grant/admin writes via SCP; review Data Lake settings and the set of LF administrators.

checks.title: Self-grant Lambda invoke via resource policy
checks.grants: Can add itself to this function's invoke policy and trigger it (runs as the exec role)
checks.why: this principal can call lambda:AddPermission on a privileged function to add itself (or an external account) to the function's invoke policy, then trigger it. The function executes as its execution role the target, so invoking it is code execution as that role - the prize is not the function but the role it surrenders and everything that role can reach. The attacker rewrites the invoke lock rather than holding an existing invoke grant.
checks.fix: Restrict lambda:AddPermission to function owners; deny invoke-policy writes via SCP; require aws:PrincipalOrgID / SourceArn on function resource policies; least-privilege the execution role.

checks.title: Self-grant S3 read via bucket policy
checks.grants: Can rewrite this bucket's policy to grant itself read access, then read it
checks.why: this principal can call s3:PutBucketPolicy on bucket the target to attach a resource policy granting itself (or the public) s3:GetObject, then read the bucket's objects. This bypasses the absence of an identity-policy read grant: the attacker rewrites the lock rather than holding a key. Severity is driven by the bucket's sensitivity - control of the policy becomes direct exfiltration of whatever the target holds.
checks.fix: Restrict s3:PutBucketPolicy to CI/CD/admins; enable account-level S3 Block Public Access; deny bucket-policy writes via SCP.

checks.title: Self-grant secret read via resource policy
checks.grants: Can rewrite this secret's resource policy to grant itself read, then read it
checks.why: this principal can call secretsmanager:PutResourcePolicy on secret the target to attach a resource policy granting itself (or the public) secretsmanager:GetSecretValue, then read the secret value. This bypasses the absence of an identity-policy read grant: the attacker rewrites the lock rather than holding a key. A secret frequently holds another principal's long-term credentials, so control of the policy becomes direct credential theft and a pivot to whatever identity the target holds.
checks.fix: Restrict secretsmanager:PutResourcePolicy to secret admins; deny resource-policy writes via SCP; require aws:PrincipalOrgID on secret resource policies.

checks.title: Self-grant SNS topic access
checks.grants: Can add an attacker account to this SNS topic's policy, then read or inject
checks.why: this principal can call sns:AddPermission to add an external account to topic the target's policy, then subscribe (read) or publish (inject). Active counterpart to public-sns-topic-policy - we detect the exposed topic today but not the identity that can create it.
checks.fix: Restrict sns:AddPermission on the topic.

checks.title: Self-grant SQS queue access
checks.grants: Can add an attacker account to this SQS queue's policy, then read or inject
checks.why: this principal can call sqs:AddPermission to grant an attacker account ReceiveMessage/SendMessage on queue the target, reading or injecting messages.
checks.fix: Restrict sqs:AddPermission and sqs:SetQueueAttributes on the queue.

checks.title: Assume role
checks.grants: Can assume this role and inherit all its permissions
checks.why: this principal can call sts:AssumeRole on the target because the target's trust policy admits it, receiving a full set of the target's temporary credentials. For the duration of that session this principal effectively becomes the target and wields every permission the target holds, and since the target is itself a principal, it can in turn assume further roles, escalating or moving laterally across the account.
checks.fix: Tighten the role trust policy; remove sts:AssumeRole from the principal.

checks.title: Authorize Redshift snapshot restore
checks.grants: Can authorize an attacker account to restore this Redshift snapshot
checks.why: this principal can call redshift:AuthorizeSnapshotAccess to authorize an attacker account to restore snapshot the target, yielding a full copy of the data warehouse. Active counterpart to the public-redshift-snapshot-shared exposure.
checks.fix: Restrict redshift:AuthorizeSnapshotAccess on the snapshot.

checks.title: Backdoor OIDC provider audience
checks.grants: Can add an attacker audience to a trusted OIDC provider
checks.why: this principal can call iam:AddClientIDToOpenIDConnectProvider to register an attacker-controlled audience on a trusted OIDC provider, then create a matching token and call sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity into role the target that trusts that provider.
checks.fix: Restrict iam:AddClientIDToOpenIDConnectProvider to a break-glass role; alarm on changes to OIDC providers.

checks.title: Batch-disable Security Hub standards
checks.grants: Can switch off compliance standards on this Security Hub without a full disable
checks.why: this principal can call securityhub:BatchDisableStandards to switch off compliance standards quietly, without the loud full-disable event.
checks.fix: Restrict securityhub:BatchDisableStandards to a break-glass role.

mitre.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools

checks.title: Connect to RDS with IAM auth token
checks.grants: Can authenticate to this RDS instance with an IAM-issued database token
checks.why: this principal can call rds-db:connect to obtain a short-lived IAM authentication token for RDS instance the target and log in as a database user, with no stored DB password. When the instance has IAM database authentication enabled, control of the IAM principal becomes data-plane access to the database - direct exfiltration of whatever it holds.
checks.fix: Disable IAM database authentication where unused; scope rds-db:connect to specific dbuser resource ARNs; prefer least-privilege DB users.

checks.title: Create access key for user
checks.grants: Can create a new long-lived access key for this user
checks.why: this principal can call iam:CreateAccessKey to create a brand-new long-lived access key for user the target without knowing any of the target's existing secrets. From then on this principal can authenticate the API as the target with that key. The key is independent of the target's other credentials, it survives a password reset or key rotation, so this is both an account-takeover and a durable persistence foothold.
checks.fix: Remove iam:CreateAccessKey from the principal.

checks.title: Create Redshift IAM DB credentials
checks.grants: Can create a temporary IAM database login and read this Redshift cluster
checks.why: this principal can call redshift:GetClusterCredentials on cluster the target to have AWS create a short-lived database username and password bound to this principal's IAM identity, then connect to the cluster and query it. This bridges an IAM-only foothold into the Redshift data plane with no stored DB password - control of the IAM principal becomes read access to whatever the warehouse holds.
checks.fix: Restrict redshift:GetClusterCredentials (and GetClusterCredentialsWithIAM); scope it to specific dbuser/dbname; prefer short-lived, audited DB roles.

checks.title: Create service-specific credential for user
checks.grants: Can create service-specific (CodeCommit/Keyspaces) credentials for this user
checks.why: this principal can call iam:CreateServiceSpecificCredential to create a fresh long-lived service-specific credential (Git-over-HTTPS for CodeCommit, or Amazon Keyspaces/Cassandra) for user the target without knowing any of the target's existing secrets. From then on this principal can authenticate to those services as the target. The credential is independent of the target's password and access keys and survives their rotation, so it is both a takeover of the target's service access and a durable persistence foothold, narrower in blast radius than a full access key.
checks.fix: Remove iam:CreateServiceSpecificCredential / iam:ResetServiceSpecificCredential from the principal.

checks.title: Decrypt with KMS key
checks.grants: Can decrypt ciphertext protected by this KMS key
checks.why: this principal can call kms:Decrypt with the target, verified against both this principal's identity policy and the target's key policy. The key is a gatekeeper: decrypt access unlocks every ciphertext the key protects (encrypted secrets, volumes, snapshots, S3 objects), so control of the key amplifies into control of all the data it gates.
checks.fix: Tighten the KMS key policy and the principal's kms:Decrypt; use grants/least-privilege key policies.

checks.title: Degrade CloudTrail configuration
checks.grants: Can repoint or degrade this trail (dead bucket, drop multi-region)
checks.why: this principal can call cloudtrail:UpdateTrail on the target to send delivery to an attacker-controlled or non-existent S3 bucket, or to turn off multi-region and global-service events. The trail is still 'logging' but the records never land anywhere useful.
checks.fix: Restrict cloudtrail:UpdateTrail to a break-glass role; deny org-wide via SCP and alarm on the event.

mitre.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Cloud Logs

checks.title: Delete CloudTrail trail
checks.grants: Can delete this CloudTrail trail outright
checks.why: this principal can call cloudtrail:DeleteTrail to remove trail the target entirely. Louder than StopLogging because the trail disappears from the console, but equally effective at ending recording - and already-delivered log files in S3 survive, so this blinds the future rather than erasing the past.
checks.fix: Restrict cloudtrail:DeleteTrail to a break-glass role; deny it org-wide via SCP and alarm on the event.

mitre.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Cloud Logs

checks.title: Delete CloudWatch alarms
checks.grants: Can delete alerting alarms so later activity raises no notification
checks.why: this principal can call cloudwatch:DeleteAlarms to remove alerting alarms so subsequent activity raises no notification.
checks.fix: Restrict cloudwatch:DeleteAlarms to a break-glass role. cloudwatch:DisableAlarmActions is a quieter variant.

mitre.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools

checks.title: Delete CloudWatch log group
checks.grants: Can destroy this log group and everything stored in it
checks.why: this principal can call logs:DeleteLogGroup on the target, deleting the group and all stored events - useful both to erase traces and to remove application/VPC/Lambda telemetry going forward. DeleteSubscriptionFilter and DeleteRetentionPolicy are quieter variants of the same lever.
checks.fix: Restrict logs:DeleteLogGroup to a break-glass role; deny via SCP and alarm on the event.

mitre.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Cloud Logs

checks.title: Delete Config delivery channel
checks.grants: Can cut this Config recorder's S3/SNS delivery
checks.why: this principal can call config:DeleteDeliveryChannel to sever where AWS Config ships its snapshots and notifications, so configuration history stops being persisted even if the recorder keeps running.
checks.fix: Restrict config:DeleteDeliveryChannel to a break-glass role; deny via SCP (no resource-level scope, so the Deny must use Resource "*").

mitre.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools

checks.title: Delete Config recorder
checks.grants: Can delete this AWS Config recorder outright
checks.why: this principal can call config:DeleteConfigurationRecorder on the target, ending configuration-history recording entirely rather than merely stopping it. Downstream Config rules and drift detection stop evaluating.
checks.fix: Restrict config:DeleteConfigurationRecorder to a break-glass role; deny via SCP (the action has no resource-level scope, so the Deny must use Resource "*").

mitre.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools

checks.title: Delete GuardDuty detector
checks.grants: Can delete this GuardDuty detector, ending threat detection in the region
checks.why: this principal can call guardduty:DeleteDetector on the target, which is the region's entire GuardDuty configuration - deleting it stops all threat detection there and discards existing findings. Nothing else in the account signals that detection has gone away.
checks.fix: Restrict guardduty:DeleteDetector / DisassociateFromMasterAccount to a break-glass role; deny via SCP and alarm on the event.

mitre.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools

checks.title: Delete IAM Access Analyzer
checks.grants: Can delete the IAM Access Analyzer, blinding external-access findings
checks.why: this principal can call access-analyzer:DeleteAnalyzer to delete the IAM Access Analyzer, blinding external- and unused-access findings so later resource-policy grants go unnoticed. Prefix is access-analyzer.
checks.fix: Restrict access-analyzer:DeleteAnalyzer to a break-glass role; deny via SCP.

mitre.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools

checks.title: Delete SCP
checks.grants: Can delete an SCP outright, removing its guardrail everywhere
checks.why: this principal can call organizations:DeletePolicy to delete an SCP outright, removing its guardrail everywhere it was attached.
checks.fix: Restrict organizations:DeletePolicy to a break-glass management-account role.

mitre.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools

checks.title: Delete VPC flow logs
checks.grants: Can delete VPC flow logs, blinding network telemetry
checks.why: this principal can call ec2:DeleteFlowLogs to remove VPC/subnet/ENI flow logs, blinding network telemetry.
checks.fix: Restrict ec2:DeleteFlowLogs to a break-glass role.

mitre.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Cloud Logs

checks.title: Delete WAFv2 WebACL
checks.grants: Can delete a WAF WebACL, dropping request filtering in front of the app
checks.why: this principal can call wafv2:DeleteWebACL to remove a WAF WebACL, dropping request filtering in front of the protected app.
checks.fix: Restrict wafv2:DeleteWebACL to a break-glass role. UpdateWebACL to default-Allow or DeleteLoggingConfiguration are variants.

mitre.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools

checks.title: Disable GuardDuty detector
checks.grants: Can disable this GuardDuty detector without deleting it
checks.why: this principal can call guardduty:UpdateDetector on the target with enable=false (or lengthen the finding-publishing frequency) to quietly turn off threat detection. Unlike DeleteDetector the detector still exists, so a config review sees it present but blind.
checks.fix: Restrict guardduty:UpdateDetector to a break-glass role; deny via SCP and alarm on the event.

mitre.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools

checks.title: Disable Security Hub
checks.grants: Can disable Security Hub in this region, ending aggregated findings
checks.why: this principal can call securityhub:DisableSecurityHub to turn off Security Hub in the region, ending aggregated findings and compliance scoring.
checks.fix: Restrict securityhub:DisableSecurityHub to a break-glass role; deny via SCP.

mitre.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools

checks.title: Invoke Lambda (run as its role)
checks.grants: Can invoke this Lambda function and run it as its execution role
checks.why: this principal can call lambda:InvokeFunction on the target, verified against both this principal's identity policy and the target's resource (invoke) policy. The function runs as its execution role, so invoking it is code execution as that role, the target is not the prize but a hinge: the chain continues to the role it surrenders (lambda-cred-theft) and everything that role can reach.
checks.fix: Scope lambda:InvokeFunction and the function's resource policy; least-privilege the execution role.

checks.title: Log group subscription exfil
checks.grants: Can stream this log group in real time to an attacker sink
checks.why: this principal can call logs:PutSubscriptionFilter on log group the target to stream every incoming log event in real time to an attacker-controlled Kinesis/Firehose/Lambda, exfiltrating application and audit logs continuously.
checks.fix: Restrict logs:PutSubscriptionFilter on the log group and iam:PassRole for the delivery role.

checks.title: Narrow CloudTrail event selectors
checks.grants: Can strip management/data events from this trail while leaving it enabled
checks.why: this principal can call cloudtrail:PutEventSelectors on trail the target to remove management or data event recording. Stealthier than StopLogging: the trail stays enabled and looks healthy on a console review, but the events the attacker cares about are no longer captured.
checks.fix: Restrict cloudtrail:PutEventSelectors to a break-glass role; deny org-wide via SCP and alarm on the event.

mitre.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Cloud Logs

checks.title: Poison an ECR image a privileged Lambda/ECS workload runs
checks.grants: Can push a malicious image to a repo a privileged Lambda/ECS workload pulls, poisoning its next launch
checks.why: this principal can call ecr:PutImage to push a malicious image to a repository that the target's workload pulls from; on the workload's next image pull the attacker's image runs as the target. Because the graph shows the current binding - not the future pull - this is a speculative artifact-poisoning finding: it bites when the consumer re-pulls (an ECS relaunch on a mutable tag; a Lambda redeploy).
checks.fix: Restrict ecr:PutImage on this repo; pin consumers to immutable digests; enable ECR tag immutability; scan images before deploy.

checks.title: Pull ECR image
checks.grants: Can pull and read images from this ECR repository
checks.why: this principal can pull images from repository the target (ecr:BatchGetImage + ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer), verified against both this principal's identity policy and the target's repository policy. Container images frequently bake in credentials, tokens and source, pulling one is data/secret exfiltration.
checks.fix: Scope ecr:BatchGetImage / ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer and the repository policy.

checks.title: Push SSH key via Instance Connect
checks.grants: Can push an SSH key via Instance Connect and log into this instance
checks.why: this principal can call ec2-instance-connect:SendSSHPublicKey to push an ephemeral SSH key onto running instance the target and then SSH in over the network, landing on the box with OS-level code execution. From there this principal reads the instance's attached IAM role credentials from IMDS and pivots further. Unlike SSM Session Manager this requires a reachable SSH port (22) on the target, so it only works where the network path exists.
checks.fix: Restrict ec2-instance-connect:SendSSHPublicKey to break-glass principals; close inbound port 22 and prefer SSM Session Manager.

checks.title: Read CloudWatch log events
checks.grants: Can read the stored log events of this CloudWatch log group
checks.why: this principal can call logs:GetLogEvents to read the stored log events of CloudWatch log group the target. Application and platform logs routinely contain access keys, bearer tokens, database connection strings and PII printed by careless code, so reading them is direct data exfiltration and, when a long-term credential is present, a pivot to whatever identity it belongs to. CloudWatch Logs is a public-endpoint, IAM-gated API, so this is a control-plane read with no network precondition; severity tracks the log group's sensitivity.
checks.fix: Restrict logs:GetLogEvents/FilterLogEvents/GetQueryResults to the principals that need them; scrub credentials/PII from logs and enable a CloudWatch Logs data-protection policy.

checks.title: Read DynamoDB table
checks.grants: Can read items from this DynamoDB table
checks.why: this principal can call dynamodb:GetItem to read items from table the target, direct exfiltration of whatever the table holds. DynamoDB is a public-endpoint, IAM-gated API, so this is a control-plane read with no network precondition. The objective, not a stepping-stone; severity tracks the table's sensitivity.
checks.fix: Restrict dynamodb:GetItem/Query/Scan to the principals that need it.

checks.title: Read EBS snapshot blocks directly
checks.grants: Can read this EBS snapshot's raw blocks directly, no volume restore
checks.why: this principal can call ebs:ListSnapshotBlocks then ebs:GetSnapshotBlock to read the raw blocks of snapshot the target over the EBS direct APIs, reconstructing the full disk without ever creating a volume. An encrypted snapshot additionally requires kms:Decrypt on its key (a split-identity path).
checks.fix: Deny ebs:GetSnapshotBlock / ListSnapshotBlocks on the snapshot; for encrypted snapshots, also restrict kms:Decrypt on the key.

checks.title: Read Glue connection JDBC credentials
checks.grants: Can read this Glue connection's stored JDBC/DB password
checks.why: this principal can call glue:GetConnection on the target; Glue connections store JDBC/database passwords, so one read returns plaintext credentials to the backing database.
checks.fix: Restrict glue:GetConnection / GetConnections; store DB credentials in Secrets Manager referenced by the connection instead of inline.

mitre.name: Credentials from Password Stores: Cloud Secrets Management Stores

checks.title: Read S3 objects
checks.grants: Can read the objects stored in this bucket
checks.why: this principal can call s3:GetObject to read the objects stored in bucket the target, verified against both this principal's identity policy and the target's bucket policy. This is the objective, not a stepping-stone: it is direct exfiltration of whatever data the target holds, the breach itself. Its severity is driven by the bucket's sensitivity, not by any further access it grants.
checks.fix: Restrict s3:GetObject and tighten the bucket policy.

checks.title: Read Secrets Manager secret
checks.grants: Can read this Secrets Manager secret value
checks.why: this principal can call secretsmanager:GetSecretValue to read the target, verified against both this principal's identity policy and the target's resource policy. A secret frequently holds another principal's long-term credentials (DB passwords, API keys, IAM access keys), so reading it is both the objective and a lateral-movement multiplier, control of the secret can become control of a new identity.
checks.fix: Scope the secret's resource policy and the principal's secretsmanager:GetSecretValue; rotate exposed secrets.

mitre.name: Credentials from Password Stores: Cloud Secrets Management Stores

checks.title: Read SSM SecureString parameter
checks.grants: Can read and decrypt this SSM SecureString parameter
checks.why: this principal can call ssm:GetParameter to read SecureString parameter the target, decrypting its value. SecureString parameters commonly store credentials, API keys and tokens, so reading one is direct credential theft and a pivot to whatever identity those credentials belong to.
checks.fix: Restrict ssm:GetParameter; prefer Secrets Manager with rotation for credentials.

mitre.name: Credentials from Password Stores: Cloud Secrets Management Stores

checks.title: Recursively dump SSM SecureString path
checks.grants: Can recursively dump every SecureString parameter under this path in one call
checks.why: this principal can call ssm:GetParametersByPath --recursive --with-decryption to read SecureString parameter the target together with every other parameter beneath its path, in a single API call. This is authorised independently of ssm:GetParameter, so a principal holding only GetParametersByPath can dump an entire credential tree even where GetParameter is denied, and it needs no prior knowledge of parameter names.
checks.fix: Restrict ssm:GetParametersByPath - it is NOT covered by denying ssm:GetParameter - and scope it to a narrow path prefix.

mitre.name: Credentials from Password Stores: Cloud Secrets Management Stores

checks.title: Reset console password for user
checks.grants: Can reset this user's console password and take it over
checks.why: this principal can call iam:UpdateLoginProfile to reset the console password of user the target that already has one, locking in a password this principal controls and gaining interactive console access as the target. Same takeover outcome as creating a profile, for a user that already had console access.
checks.fix: Remove iam:UpdateLoginProfile from the principal.

checks.title: Reset RDS master password
checks.grants: Can reset the master password on this live RDS instance
checks.why: this principal can call rds:ModifyDBInstance on the target to set a new MasterUserPassword, then connect as the master user and read everything. No snapshot or IAM-auth needed; the only gate is network reachability.
checks.fix: Restrict rds:ModifyDBInstance on the instance; alarm on MasterUserPassword changes.

checks.title: Rotate access key to create credentials for user
checks.grants: Can rotate out a key to create a new access key for this user
checks.why: this principal can call iam:DeleteAccessKey to remove one of user the target's existing access keys and then iam:CreateAccessKey to create a brand-new long-lived key under this principal's control, without knowing any of the target's secrets. Unlike plain key creating, the added delete bypasses AWS's two-access-key-per-user limit, so this works even when the target already holds the maximum of two keys. From then on this principal authenticates the API as the target; the new key is independent of the target's other credentials, so it is both an account takeover and a durable persistence foothold.
checks.fix: Remove iam:CreateAccessKey and iam:DeleteAccessKey from the principal.

checks.title: S3 replication exfil
checks.grants: Can configure replication to copy this bucket out to an attacker bucket
checks.why: this principal can call s3:PutReplicationConfiguration on bucket the target to set up continuous replication to an attacker-owned destination bucket, exfiltrating every current and future object out of band.
checks.fix: Restrict s3:PutReplicationConfiguration on the bucket and iam:PassRole for the replication role.

checks.title: Schedule KMS key deletion
checks.grants: Can schedule this KMS key for deletion, destroying everything it encrypts
checks.why: this principal can call kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion on customer-managed key the target. Once the waiting period elapses the key material is destroyed and every object, snapshot, secret and parameter encrypted under it becomes permanently unreadable - a one-call, account-wide data-destruction move that no backup of the ciphertext can undo. Deleting the key also blinds anything that depended on decrypting with it.
checks.fix: Restrict kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion to key administrators; deny it via SCP outside a break-glass role.

checks.title: Set console password for user
checks.grants: Can set a console password for this user that had none
checks.why: this principal can call iam:CreateLoginProfile to set a console password for user the target that currently has none (e.g. a programmatic-only service user). That gives this principal interactive AWS console access as the target, a takeover of an account that previously had no human login path, and the password persists until changed.
checks.fix: Remove iam:CreateLoginProfile from the principal.

checks.title: Share AMI out
checks.grants: Can share this AMI out to an attacker account
checks.why: this principal can call ec2:ModifyImageAttribute on the target to share the AMI with an attacker-controlled account. Images routinely bake in data, source and credentials, so sharing one exfiltrates whatever it holds, and lets the attacker launch instances from it in their own account.
checks.fix: Restrict ec2:ModifyImageAttribute; review AMI launchPermission sharing.

checks.title: Share Aurora cluster snapshot out
checks.grants: Can share this Aurora cluster snapshot out to an attacker account
checks.why: this principal can call rds:ModifyDBClusterSnapshotAttribute to share an Aurora cluster snapshot the target with an attacker account. The existing rds-snapshot-share rule covers only instance snapshots, so Aurora clusters are a blind spot today.
checks.fix: Restrict rds:ModifyDBClusterSnapshotAttribute on the cluster snapshot.

checks.title: Share EBS snapshot out
checks.grants: Can share this EBS snapshot out to an attacker account
checks.why: this principal can call ec2:ModifySnapshotAttribute on the target to add an attacker-controlled account to its createVolumePermission, sharing a full disk copy out of the account. This bypasses every control on the live volume: the attacker restores the snapshot in their own account and reads it at leisure.
checks.fix: Restrict ec2:ModifySnapshotAttribute; deny createVolumePermission changes via SCP/policy.

checks.title: Share RDS snapshot out
checks.grants: Can share this RDS snapshot out to an attacker account
checks.why: this principal can call rds:ModifyDBSnapshotAttribute on the target to share a full database copy with an attacker-controlled account, exfiltration that bypasses the live DB's network and auth controls (the attacker restores the snapshot in their own account).
checks.fix: Restrict rds:ModifyDBSnapshotAttribute; deny restore/share changes via SCP/policy.

checks.title: Snapshot EBS volume for exfil
checks.grants: Can snapshot this EBS volume and read the copy elsewhere
checks.why: this principal can call ec2:CreateSnapshot on the target to take a full point-in-time copy of the disk, then restore or share that copy out of band. Unlike detach-and-reattach this needs one permission, no instance in the volume's Availability Zone, and does not disturb the running workload - which makes it the quieter and far more common route to the same data.
checks.fix: Restrict ec2:CreateSnapshot to backup automation; encrypt volumes with a CMK the principal cannot use, and deny ec2:ModifySnapshotAttribute so a copy cannot be shared out.

checks.title: Steal EBS volume by reattachment
checks.grants: Can detach this EBS volume and reattach it to an attacker-controlled instance
checks.why: this principal can call ec2:DetachVolume on the target and ec2:AttachVolume to reattach it to an instance it controls, then mount and read the filesystem offline. This bypasses every OS-level and application-level control on the original host - no snapshot is created and no data-plane credential is needed, the disk simply changes owner.
checks.fix: Restrict ec2:DetachVolume / ec2:AttachVolume to the instances and volumes that need them; encrypt volumes with a CMK the principal cannot use.

checks.title: Stop AWS Config recorder
checks.grants: Can stop this AWS Config recorder, ending configuration history
checks.why: this principal can call config:StopConfigurationRecorder on the target, halting AWS Config's recording of resource configuration changes. Config rules stop evaluating and the configuration timeline goes blank, so subsequent changes leave no configuration-history trace even though CloudTrail may still record the API calls.
checks.fix: Restrict config:StopConfigurationRecorder to a break-glass role; deny it via SCP (the action has no resource-level scope, so the Deny must use Resource "*").

mitre.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools

checks.title: Stop CloudTrail logging
checks.grants: Can stop this CloudTrail trail from recording API activity
checks.why: this principal can call cloudtrail:StopLogging on trail the target, halting management- and data-event recording without deleting anything. The trail still exists and still looks configured, so the gap is easy to miss on a console review, and every action the attacker takes afterwards goes unrecorded in that trail.
checks.fix: Restrict cloudtrail:StopLogging to a break-glass role; deny it org-wide via SCP and alarm on the event.

mitre.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Cloud Logs

checks.title: Strip MFA from user
checks.grants: Can remove the MFA device from this user, weakening it for takeover
checks.why: this principal can call iam:DeactivateMFADevice on user the target, removing the MFA requirement on that identity. Combined with a password reset or access-key create this turns a partially-protected account into a fully usable one.
checks.fix: Remove iam:DeactivateMFADevice from the principal; restrict MFA administration to a break-glass role and alarm on the event.

checks.title: Take over a SAML provider to assume trusting roles
checks.grants: Can replace the SAML provider this role trusts, forging federated logins as it
checks.why: this principal can call iam:UpdateSAMLProvider to replace the SAML metadata document that the target trusts, making attacker-created SAML assertions valid. It then calls sts:AssumeRoleWithSAML to assume the target directly - that STS call is authorised by the target's trust policy (which already trusts the provider), not by any identity permission, so no secondary action is needed. If the target is privileged this is a full federation takeover.
checks.fix: Restrict iam:UpdateSAMLProvider to break-glass admins; alarm on it (CloudTrail); pin role trust to specific SAML attributes.

checks.title: Take over an OIDC provider to assume trusting roles
checks.grants: Can re-point the OIDC provider this role trusts, forging federated logins as it
checks.why: this principal can call iam:UpdateOpenIDConnectProviderThumbprint to change the trusted thumbprint of the OIDC provider the target trusts (or add a client ID), making tokens from an attacker-controlled IdP valid. It then calls sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity to assume the target directly - authorised by the target's trust policy, not by any identity permission. If the target is privileged this is a full federation takeover.
checks.fix: Restrict iam:UpdateOpenIDConnectProviderThumbprint / iam:AddClientIDToOpenIDConnectProvider to break-glass admins; alarm on them (CloudTrail); pin role trust to specific sub/aud claims.
